quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is okay to drag your feet on the ground.
Your toes should point downward.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag them on the ground. Do not point your toes down, as they may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and learn the shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and learn the shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Blocks your side vision.
Greatly reduces the severity of head injury.
Is usually uncomfortable.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Greatly reduces the severity of head injury.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:

options.text: Fits snugly.
Is well-worn and broken in.
Is loose.
Does not have a chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible defects.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
About once every 10 rides.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to stay out of blind spots, improve visibility, avoid road hazards, avoid wind from other vehicles, and have an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
Brakes on both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: To reduce your accident risk, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you very closely.
Look only at your controls, not ahead.
Signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Should be avoided.
Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is unsafe because turn signals don't work.
Should only happen in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night to make yourself more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should be near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group if they lead.
They will ride too fast otherwise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: In a group, less experienced riders should ride toward the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them easily.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that allows you to draft off other vehicles.
The one that allows other motorists to see you.
The one that places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that allows other motorists to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where you can see others and others can see you. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards on the road. Your position should prevent other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed. Choose a position that gives you the most space around you.

questions.question: What does space between your motorcycle and other vehicles provide?

options.text: Time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you in one area of the lane with limited movement.
Lets you rely on others to identify hazards.
Requires you to go faster to stay with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: How often does a motorcycle need attention?

options.text: Less often than a car.
More often than a car.
Only by a mechanic before each ride.
Only at a dealership.

questions.correctAnswerText: More often than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do?

options.text: Changes lane position as conditions change.
Stays in one part of the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist has three lane position choices. Choose the safest position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a crash?

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Those familiar with their motorcycle.
Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle have the most crashes.

questions.question: What happens when you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is fine as long as you are under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is fine as long as no other vehicles are near.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not be able to hold the turn and could end up in another lane or off the road. Use caution when turning.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid a slippery surface?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: It is too dangerous for inexperienced riders.
Use it by itself.
Use it to occasionally help the rear brake.
Use it together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots too small to cause problems.
Have blind spots that need head checks.
Have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that need head checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What best protects you while riding?

options.text: Sunglasses
Goggles
A windshield
A face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. Sunglasses or a windshield do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it can finish before another vehicle appears.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones mean no passing. You also cannot pass by riding on the shoulder.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to create distance.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Safe when used correctly.
Safe even if used incorrectly.
Only for use if the rear brake fails.
Not for regular use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe when used correctly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides most of your stopping power.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect like:

options.text: Using the brakes.
Accelerating.
Swerving.
Turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows you down like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen better.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space should:

options.text: Always stay the same.
Change based on riding conditions.
Not be used in most situations.
Be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more time to stop, if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently, you should:

options.text: Continue riding normally.
Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in handling may mean a tire has failed. If your motorcycle feels different, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be in your body.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system. This can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean when the operator leans.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you check before riding?

options.text: Tire wear and tread
Seat cushion comfort
Paint shine
Wind direction

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire wear and tread
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up.
Leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may just make them tailgate you faster.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Wear bright-colored clothing.
Wear dark clothing.
Ride without your headlight.
Weave in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen during daylight, always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Use the same lane position all the time.
Change lane positions often to stay alert.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change all the time, so the safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers see you best.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: At night.
During the day.
At dusk.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and bright-colored clothing when riding. Crashes happen in daylight and at night, so be highly visible at all times.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Guarantees you won't be arrested for drinking and riding.
Guarantees alcohol won't affect your riding.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's alcohol per hour. But the time needed varies. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane all the time.
Weave between lane positions to keep drivers out of their lane.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What type of sign can be rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow them.

questions.question: Which surface gives good traction for tires?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement gives good traction for motorcycle tires.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see far to the sides for safe riding
It looks good
It does not have a chin strap
It protects your hearing

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see far to the sides for safe riding
questions.explanation: A helmet approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation will not limit your vision. You will be able to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Only at night
Only during the day
Never
Day and night

questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps others see you at any time. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing both day and night.

questions.question: What footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that support your ankles provide the best protection. Laced-up boots or high-top shoes work well. If your laces are long, tuck them away before riding.

questions.question: What does a properly-fitted motorcycle allow you to do?

options.text: Touch the ground with your feet while seated
Have the seat even with your waist
Have the seat 10 inches above your waist
Have the seat 10 inches below your waist

questions.correctAnswerText: Touch the ground with your feet while seated
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets you touch the ground with your feet while you sit on it. Keep your feet on the footrests when riding.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Never
Occasionally
Frequently
More often than you look ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see what is behind you. This helps you spot dangers early.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?

options.text: THC
TMJ
MRT
AAP

questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: The main active ingredient in marijuana is THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

questions.question: What should you NOT check before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Making sure the headlight works
Checking the oil level
Testing both brakes to make sure the brake light works
Checking if the paint is scratched

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking if the paint is scratched
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and all lights (headlight, taillight, signals, and brake light). You do not need to check the paint.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen best?

options.text: Orange and red
Green and blue
Purple and gold
Black and white

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red
questions.explanation: Wear clothing in bright orange, red, yellow, or green to make yourself visible to other drivers.
